Marta: Quick thread to finalize the migration lane runbook + credit structures for model catalog transitions. Need final thumbs on benchmarks, pin behaviour, comm cadence, and migration financial incentives. High-level proposal below.

Ravi: Drop the proposal pls. We need concrete numbers for benchmarks and a rollback playbook.

Marta: Pasting proposal. Feedback welcome.
```text
Proposal summary:
- Lanes:
  * rapid: 3-14d, automated eval only, small cohort
  * standard: 30d canary with phased traffic (customer opt-in)
  * extended: 60d canary + manual QA for sensitive customers
  * enterprise: custom timeline + SLA + freeze-window option

- Pin behavior:
  * rolling-pin: model stays pinned for 30d (soft), becomes eligible for automatic swap after 30d unless customer requests extension
  * grace-pin: 90d opt-out window, after which model retires unless enterprise exception
  * permanent: enterprise-only, contract-level pin forever

- Credits/incentives:
  * cutover within 45d: 2 months service credits (applied to next invoice)
  * cutover within 90d: 1 month credit
  * participation in canary + bug reports: $500 one-time credits for qualified accounts

- Benchmarks (must pass all automated checks for rollout):
  * embeddings: holdout cosine drift <= 0.012 OR ROC-AUC delta <= 0.01
  * generation: avg NLL delta <= 0.25 and human eval delta <= 1.0 point on prioritized prompts
  * latency: p95 < 180ms for 50-token baseline in prod-like region
  * stability: no new errors > 0.2% of requests over baseline

- Rollout cadence & canary percentages: [1%, 5%, 25%, 60%] with 24-72h observation windows.

- Notifications: day 0 notice, 21d reminder, 10d, 3d, 1d, and final deprecation reminder 24h before hard retire.

- Rollback triggers (observable):
  * lat p95 increase > 15% OR absolute increase > 50ms
  * quality regression vs baseline > 1.5% (automated metric) OR human eval drift > 2 points
  * error rate spike > 0.5%
  * legal/compliance flag via legal-bot

- Special ops: enterprise freeze-window (optionally stop auto-swap for contract length), manual switchboard for customer-critical flows.
```

Jordan: Looks solid. Two asks: 1) include per-tenant delta logging so we can measure blast radius, 2) add a small smoke-test harness that runs a fixed prompt set post-switch.

Marta: Adding both. Updated benchmarks include smoke-test pass (>=95% on smoke prompts).

Lina: CS/Sales note: credit terms must be non-refundable and applied as invoice credit; we should have a template offer. Also need a migration checklist one-pager and an engineer-run runbook.

Kofi: Infra ops: what about cost neutral fallback? If new model increases token cost > 10%, we should auto-fallback or route lower-tier traffic to a cheaper compatible variant. Also need a flag for disabled KV cache during canaries to detect regressions.

Marta: Agree on cost threshold. Add to rollback triggers: token cost delta > 10% sustained over 24h. Also note we can set cache-mode: "canary-safe" which hashes to separate cache namespace.

legal-bot: Reminder: For enterprise contracts, any permanent pin must be captured in SOW and countersigned. Migration credits are marketing spend; route to finance approval pipeline.

Ravi: Can we show a sample rollout YAML that the runtime team can ingest?

Marta: Sure, quick draft below.
```yaml
rollout:
  lane: standard
  steps:
    - pct: 1
      wait: 48h
    - pct: 5
      wait: 48h
    - pct: 25
      wait: 72h
    - pct: 60
      wait: 72h
  smoke_tests: true
  alerts:
    latency_p95_pct: 15
    latency_p95_absolute_ms: 50
    quality_drop_pct: 1.5
    error_rate_pct: 0.5
    token_cost_pct: 10
  cache_mode: canary-safe
  per_tenant_logging: true
```
deploy-bot: Started canary for catalog:v4 in eu-central at 2026-04-02T09:21Z :construction:

Marta: Next steps:
- Jordan to own smoke-test harness + sample prompt set (due Thu)
- Kofi to add cache_mode + cost-check hooks in runtime (due Fri)
- Lina + Sales to create credit & one-pager templates (due Mon)
- Legal to add SOW language draft (legal-bot)
- I'll assemble RFC and timeline after we have artifacts.

Ravi: Fine by me. One more: please include a post-migration survey to capture CSAT and open issues.

Marta: Good call. We'll include a 10-question CSAT + bug capture link in the final comms.

Lina: I'll own the survey and the customer-facing migration checklist.

Marta: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with the RFC and schedule a 30-min exec sync next week. :calendar:
